o.text: Borrowed from Russian кит (kit), from Old Church Slavonic китъ (kitŭ), ultimately from Ancient Greek κῆτος (kêtos).
From yığ- + -ın, ultimately from Proto-Turkic *yïgïn (“heap, pile”).
From açıq + -ça. Calque of Russian открытка (otkrytka).
Derivation of Proto-Turkic *sov- + -ul. The underived form is unattested.
